chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali ibn Asbat and al-Hajjal that they heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:
One of the worshippers from the Children of Israel did not engage in worship until he remained silent for ten years.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of silence in the worship of the Children of Israel according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) narrates that a devout worshipper from the Children of Israel practiced ten years of silence before engaging in active worship, highlighting the virtue of silence as a prerequisite for spiritual devotion. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on *samt* (silence) not merely as absence of speech, but as a disciplined period of internal purification and self-reflection necessary to prevent the tongue from causing spiritual harm. It reflects the broader scholarly view that mastery of the self through silence is foundational to the efficacy of subsequent acts of worship.
